PullRequest.Title: perf: reduce chat rendering overhead with compositor-driven Draw

## Summary

Reduce redundant rendering and component-lifetime retention when several chat sessions are active. Related to #340236, but this is not a claim that the full reported layout regression is resolved.

- Move Draw from per-frame SVG path updates to **Atlas 120**: 320 sampled poses over the unchanged 2,667 ms cycle, played by native stepped compositor transforms. Generate padded atlases at the actual icon size, device pixel ratio, and resolved theme color; share in-flight generation and resources through a per-window cache with a 16 MiB decoded-source-pixel budget.
- Preserve visibility, activity, reduced-motion, no-icon, and disposal behavior. Cancel obsolete requests on theme/DPR changes and release the cache when its last owner leaves. Keep assembled SVG artwork for static states and a **60 FPS SVG fallback** during preparation or on explicitly logged atlas failures.
- Fix the rounded left ribbon tips being clipped at the transition from the held logo to the animated masks. The canonical face artwork and animation duration remain unchanged.
- Retain the existing visibility-aware **30 FPS managed-shimmer** behavior across progress, thinking, tools, subagents, transcript loading, and Agents-window session titles. **The atlas update makes no further shimmer changes; Draw no longer uses that clock.**
- Rotate static input-border gradients behind fixed masks instead of animating the gradient angle. Clip the decorative masks so their oversized gradients do not enlarge ancestor scroll bounds.
- Coalesce identical pet sprite frames while preserving the original poses and 800/1,200 ms holds; synchronize eyes with the body, cache unchanged gaze/accessory updates, suspend invisible surfaces, and use translation during dragging to avoid synchronous layout.
- Release removed toolbar dropdown references and visibility subscriptions; propagate context only to current action views.
- Reuse unchanged thinking-title markdown DOM, including correct invalidation for mutable markdown options/metadata and expansion changes.
- Skip persistent-footer row-height measurements when an update leaves the rendered progress unchanged.

Adds/extends regression coverage for these rendering and ownership paths. No dependency manifests, new settings, persistent-progress configuration defaults, pet sprite assets, or screenshot baseline hashes change. The pixel spinner is unchanged. Atlas 120 is a source sampling density, not a forced 120 Hz JavaScript loop or a guarantee that every display presents 120 frames/s.

## Performance evidence

### Production Draw atlas

The native production-component probe verified five shared-atlas widgets, accelerated transform layers, and **zero steady-state renderer Layout, UpdateLayoutTree, Paint, or FireAnimationFrame events**. A separate real Code OSS workbench smoke run used five independently connected local mock requests: all five displayed the production atlas, shared one resource, advanced their native timelines, and removed their playback surfaces when the editors closed.

A matched production-source 60/120 comparison on an M2 Pro used five visible 12 CSS-pixel logos at DPR 2, six counterbalanced samples per option and six static controls. Only the frame-count constant was changed in the isolated 60 Hz candidate; the product remains at 120. Each primary measurement followed atlas readiness, GC, and three seconds of warmup, then measured 5.334 seconds without tracing or per-frame polling.

| Metric, median of six samples | Atlas 120 (selected) | Atlas 60 candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Renderer main-thread task time | 2.18 ms/s | 0.89 ms/s |
| GPU-process CPU time | 61.66 ms/s | 46.44 ms/s |
| Background atlas readiness after component startup | 447 ms | 208 ms |
| Shared decoded source atlas at the tested size | 1,003,520 bytes | 501,760 bytes |

The 60 candidate saved about 1.28 renderer ms/s and 24.7% of GPU-process CPU time in this isolated comparison. Both had zero steady-state layout/paint/RAF events, and their native held-pose screenshots were byte-identical. We retain 120 to preserve more motion detail on higher-refresh displays; the compositor presents at its available cadence rather than forcing 120 redraws on a 60 Hz screen.

These are **component measurements, not whole-app CPU, hardware GPU utilization, battery savings, or a fresh final-branch-versus-main workbench benchmark**. Earlier production batches had higher/noisier absolute renderer totals; compare within matched batches rather than combining their numbers. Other workbench animations can also keep the compositor active. The cache budget accounts for decoded source pixels, not total GPU/process memory; temporary canvases, encoded images, and per-layer overhead are additional. Background preparation is not chat response latency, and SVG fallback remains animated while it runs.

### Earlier workbench and component measurements

The following measurements predate the atlas integration. They describe the earlier animation/pet improvements, not a newly measured aggregate percentage for the final PR. Values are renderer main-thread task milliseconds per wall-clock second on an M2 Pro.

| Workload | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Five visible chats waiting (~75 Hz original cadence) | 267.4 ms/s | 194.0 ms/s |
| Five visible chats, moderate streaming | 428.3 ms/s | 387.3 ms/s |
| Idle pet | 8.39 ms/s | 2.50 ms/s |
| Working pet | 8.97 ms/s | 4.26 ms/s |
| Pet clipped outside its viewport | 8.83 ms/s | 0.11 ms/s |

These are three-sample diagnostic comparisons of actual component/rendering paths, not release-level statistical claims. Additional checks:

- 305 toolbar overflow cycles and full GC: **307 -> 1** retained dropdown objects.
- 300 identical thinking-title updates: **300 -> 1** markdown renders; a genuinely changed title still renders.
- Native pet dragging: **288 -> 0** layouts inside steady-state pointer handlers. Total drag CPU timing was noisy, so no general CPU improvement is claimed.
- Eight-file tool scenario: **16 -> 0** redundant progress-triggered height measurements. A counterbalanced three-sample-per-condition comparison found no significant total request-layout-duration improvement (37.67 -> 37.06 ms; p=0.54).

The original multi-second GC stalls and all possible application DOM retention remain unproven. In one retained CI text-only pair from #340236, roughly 67% of the extra layout duration occurred before the request started; these response-rendering changes cannot explain or fix the whole issue. No CI metric changes or speculative startup/layout rewrites are included.

Atlas coverage includes resource sharing and bounds, pending-generation cancellation, late-result disposal, failed-request retry, source-frame fidelity and padding, hidden/remount behavior, reduced motion, theme/DPR replacement, no-icon/inactive states, and logged SVG fallback. Native component probes and the real five-chat workbench smoke also passed.

### October 13 merge and feedback validation

Merged `main` at `68343b4619b` in signed merge commit `49f739bef80`, preserving both sides of the toolbar and pet test conflicts. Fixed the selected review comment: the border regression test is a sibling of the gutter test, rather than being registered inside it.

- `npm exec --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -- bash scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.test.ts --grep '^ChatInputPart working borders rotate fixed gradients inside masks at any input aspect ratio$' --reporter spec` — **1 independently discovered test passed**.
- `npm exec --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -- bash scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/toolbar/toolbar.test.ts --run src/vs/base/test/browser/animationSync.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatPetWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatProgressAnimation.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatWorkingLogo.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatThinkingContentPart.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatToolProgressPart.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --reporter dot` — **1,374 passed, 2 existing pending**.
- Client build/typecheck, changed-file ESLint, merge-commit signing, and pre-commit hygiene passed at that revision.

### Cross-browser and inline-chat CI follow-up

Commits `eafb7800b7b` and `f0d27923970` fixed the failures found after the merge:

- Account for 1/64 CSS-pixel layout quantization and computed-style serialization in the border-size test, add fractional dimensions, and wait for the browser test runner's asynchronous stylesheet imports.
- Fix a real screenshot regression rather than accept its baseline: the large rotating gradient leaked into ancestor scroll bounds even when masked/transparent, causing focus to shift the inline-chat composer upward. `overflow: clip` on the decorative mask removes that overflow without clipping the input itself. Tests cover active/idle and compact/non-compact inputs.
- Preserve the new upstream attachment-session test while merging `main` at `b0e941623ad`.

Validation at that revision:

- `npm exec --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -- npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --browser webkit --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.test.ts --reporter dot` — **4 passed in each browser**.
- `npm exec --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -- bash scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts --reporter dot` — **803 passed, 1 existing pending**.
- Client build/typecheck, changed-file ESLint, CSS stylelint, and Light/Dark inline-chat fixture checks passed. **No screenshot baseline hashes were changed.**

On `f0d27923970`, GitHub CI passed Screenshots & Tests, Screenshots, Playwright Fixture Tests, macOS Browser, Linux Browser, all Electron-Unit platforms, and Compile & Hygiene. Separate Linux smoke failures involved a timeout and a settings-editor click; they were not addressed through unrelated source changes. These historical results are not a claim that CI for the new atlas commit has passed.

Not run for the atlas update: Windows/Linux live rendering or hardware-power/battery measurements, a complete post-patch production comparison of all eight regressed scenarios, or a matched reproduction of the original long user workload/GC stalls. Universal native OS-hide/minimize suspension is not claimed: production uses document/intersection and widget lifecycle signals, and the isolated Electron hide/minimize probe did not always report a hidden document. The component-explorer service was unavailable for the atlas follow-up; native production-component and real-workbench checks provided the live evidence instead. Performance scripts, traces, heap snapshots, and videos remain local investigation artifacts, not product files.

## Manual testing

1. Run five concurrent sessions; type, scroll, switch sessions, and resize while waiting, streaming, and using tools.
2. Inspect Draw at normal size on ordinary- and high-refresh displays. Check that the rounded left tips remain consistent at the held-to-moving transition and that the cycle does not change speed.
3. Change theme/custom progress colors, zoom, and monitor/DPR while requests run. Check correct colors and sharp edges, without stale atlases, neighboring-frame bleed, or a changed icon footprint.
4. Scroll running indicators offscreen, switch sessions, hide/reopen Chat, then cancel/complete/restart requests. Check Draw and the unchanged shimmer resume and stop correctly.
5. Toggle reduced motion during a request and exercise monochrome/no-icon modes. Reduced motion should show the assembled static logo; no-icon mode should not allocate an atlas.
6. Inspect the input border in narrow/wide layouts and Light/Dark/High Contrast, including inline chat gaining focus without shifting its composer.
7. Exercise pet idle/working transitions, gaze/accessories, dragging/throwing near edges, zoom/resize, and hidden disable/re-enable.
8. Expand/collapse thinking during updates; verify real title changes, formatting, links, and focus remain correct.
9. Resize toolbars into/out of overflow repeatedly, then open submenus and invoke actions after changing the selected item/session. Smoke-test a non-Chat toolbar too.

## Draft status

Remains a draft. The branch contains the merge-conflict, test-discovery, screenshot/browser, rounded-tail, and Atlas 120 fixes without rewriting history. Local validation passed; GitHub CI for the updated head and broader cross-platform/performance review must complete before marking it ready for review.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The hide-to-clear-to-last-reference-disposal-to-320-frame-generation call path is explicit and the single-logo hide/reveal scenario is covered by the added test. Exact duration varies by hardware and icon size, but the repeated work and trigger do not.
Findings.PerformanceResource: 320 SVG serializations and image decodes, canvas pixel buffers, and atlas encoding work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The full atlas-generation cost repeats once for every transition from zero visible Draw logos back to any visible Draw logo; simultaneous same-key logos coalesce, but sequential session switches, panel hide/show, or scrolling the only active logo out and back do not.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: repeated background CPU and allocation/GC pressure while navigating active chats
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Draw used the existing SVG artwork directly and visibility changes only stopped and restarted frame updates; there was no 320-frame resource to regenerate after each reveal.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each visible logo now owns an atlas reference, and releasing the last reference immediately disposes the per-window store and all cached atlases. The next visible logo must create a new cache entry and rerun atlas generation.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `if (--owner.references === 0) { owner.store.dispose(); }` at lines 153-154 ties cache lifetime to currently acquired/visible playback references rather than to the window or live widget lifetime; before this PR no atlas regeneration existed.
Findings.Title: Keep the bounded atlas cache across transient invisibility
Findings.Impact: With a single active request, scrolling its footer out of view, switching chat sessions, or hiding and reopening Chat destroys the warm atlas and makes the next reveal serialize/rasterize up to 320 poses and encode/load the sheet again. This adds avoidable CPU/GC activity to common navigation and keeps the SVG fallback running during every rebuild.
Findings.Evidence: `observeVisibility` calls `restartDrawAnimation` on every intersection/document visibility transition; `restartDrawAnimation` calls `clearAtlas`, which disposes the acquired reference. This added line then disposes the shared store when that was the last visible owner. Disposing the store destroys `ChatWorkingLogoAtlasCache`; the next acquire reaches `createChatWorkingLogoAtlas`, whose loop processes 320 frames with SVG serialization, object-URL image loads, canvas draw/getImageData/putImageData, and a final `toBlob`. The live-atlas test explicitly exercises hide then reveal for a single logo, which follows this cold path.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the existing 16 MiB LRU cache alive across transient zero-reference periods—e.g. own it for the window/widget lifetime or use a delayed idle teardown—and retain the current pagehide/window-unregister disposal. Playback references can still be released immediately while decoded atlases remain bounded and reusable.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Responsive relayout appended each newly created submenu/dropdown view item to a toolbar-lifetime array and kept its visibility subscription in a toolbar-lifetime store, so removed overflow generations remained reachable.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Repeated toolbar overflow/restore cycles retained an ever-growing number of obsolete dropdown objects and listeners.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The PR tracks current dropdown subscriptions in a DisposableMap and deletes/disposes the entry whenever ActionBar pulls that view item, bounding retention to current rendered items.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base declaration at line 103 owns the accumulating `submenuActionViewItems`; the deleted creation path pushed every replacement into it and the old store retained listeners until toolbar disposal. The new `pullAction` path at line 769 calls `deleteAndDispose(viewItem)`, and the added regression test verifies removed dropdowns receive no later context updates after repeated responsive overflow.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Every response-model activity notification unconditionally called `fireItemHeightChange`, which synchronously measured `rowContainer.getBoundingClientRect().height` even when persistent footer content and active state were unchanged.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Background tool/subagent activity caused redundant chat-row layout measurements and downstream height reconciliation.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: `updateWorkingContent` now reports whether rendered progress changed, and the renderer measures/reconciles height only for a changed footer or initial creation.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The blamed base line is the old unconditional `fireItemHeightChange`. Its implementation uses `getBoundingClientRect` when no measured height is supplied. The added conditional at line 2385 suppresses that call for unchanged persistent content, and the new test drives five background activity changes and observes zero measurements.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each drag pointer move wrote `left`/`top` and then computed drag resistance through geometry reads, forcing synchronous layout after the position write on the high-frequency pointer path.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Pet dragging performed repeated layout work and could become janky as pointermove frequency increased.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The PR computes geometry before mutation and moves the active drag with compositor-friendly `translate`, committing `left`/`top` only once on release.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The blamed base line is one of the per-move `left`/`top` writes; the deleted path then called `_updateDragWiggle`, which read element geometry. The changed line 2209 uses `style.translate` during drag, and the added test sends multiple moves and verifies no button-bound reads occur in the animation-frame movement path before the final commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: An active chat displays the Draw working logo, then the logo is scrolled offscreen, its session is switched away, or Chat is hidden and later revealed.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The SVG fallback starts immediately, so atlas preparation is not required for the response UI to progress; native atlas playback waits for generation and image load. Although backgrounded via idle/yields, generation consumes renderer CPU and allocations that can contend with interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Generate a 320-pose atlas by serializing SVG, loading each changed frame through an object URL, rasterizing/readback into canvases, then encoding and loading the final blob.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One 320-frame generation per cold [physical width, physical height, resolved color] key. Simultaneously visible identical logos share one promise/resource, but each zero-visible-to-visible cycle is cold because the last release disposes the whole cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The SVG logo resumed directly after visibility changes; no atlas serialization/rasterization/encoding boundary existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the immediate response-rendering critical path because the SVG fallback continues, but it adds repeated renderer CPU/GC pressure during navigation and delays transition to compositor-only playback.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of transitions from zero visible Draw logos back to a visible logo, multiplied by distinct size/DPR/color keys; each cold key performs up to 320 frame iterations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-key generation is coalesced for overlapping visible widgets. Distinct keys can generate independently under the 16 MiB decoded-source budget. Sequential session/visibility transitions are not coalesced because zero references destroys the cache.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Positive entries are LRU/budget bounded while at least one playback reference exists. Pending entries cancel when their last reference leaves. The entire per-window cache, including completed reusable entries, is disposed at zero references; failures are removed and can retry on a later acquisition.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: visibility calls clearAtlas, reference disposal tears down the last-owner store, and the next acquire runs the explicit 320-frame factory loop.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact generation time and user-visible contention vary by hardware, DPR, and navigation timing, but the 320-frame repeated-work mechanism is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium cache-lifecycle regression: transient invisibility defeats the new bounded cache and repeats heavyweight atlas generation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Visible chat progress, thinking/tool labels, transcript loading, and Agents session titles shimmer while rows enter and leave view.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A shared setTimeout/requestAnimationFrame cadence updates paused CSS animation currentTime at 30 FPS. Work is on the renderer animation path only while visible; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible managed shimmer elements and animations in their subtrees; hidden/clipped rows are removed from frame scheduling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One timer and one requestAnimationFrame queue per window coalesce wakeups, then one bounded runner executes per visible registered element. There is no cross-window sharing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Animation handles are collected on start/visibility and cleared on disposal; there is no data cache or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the scheduling path and 30 FPS bound.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Per-frame style/paint cost depends on visible labels and browser rendering, but cadence and visibility bounds are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff shares wakeups, lowers update cadence, and stops clipped/hidden work; per-visible-element sampling remains bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: The chat pet idles, tracks the cursor, becomes clipped, changes state/accessory, and is dragged across the chat surface.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible sprite timers draw distinct poses; intersection/document visibility suspends timers and gaze work. Drag pointer moves read geometry before applying compositor translation, with left/top committed on release.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load/decode packaged pet sprite-sheet and accessory images through existing FileAccess URLs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged browser-cached resource loads per distinct state/accessory URL; the diff changes frame metadata and draw frequency, not URLs or source assets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same sprite and accessory resources were loaded for the same states.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A newly selected state still waits for its image as before; the diff does not add resource requests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Pointer-event frequency while dragging/tracking, visible pet surfaces, and distinct state transitions; idle/rendering poses are reduced from 50 timer steps to two equivalent poses.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active sprite timer and one gaze animation-frame scheduler per pet; invisible surfaces cancel/suppress both. Drag moves are handled serially on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Browser image caching and existing loaded-image reuse remain; unchanged gaze/accessory states now skip DOM/canvas rewrites.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the changed timer, visibility, translation, and frame-index paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Layout and draw savings depend on pet enablement and interaction frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: pose coalescing, visibility suspension, unchanged-gaze caching, and translation-based dragging reduce hot-path work without a new scaling boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat response activity updates persistent progress footers and repeated tools update a thinking title.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Model notifications synchronously decide whether footer DOM changed; unchanged content now skips row-height measurement. Thinking titles compare cloned markdown value/metadata before markdown parsing and DOM replacement. No external boundary is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Background tool/subagent activity notifications and count of appended tools sharing the same title.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates are serialized on the renderer/UI thread; no burst of asynchronous boundary calls exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The footer uses current rendered state as its deduplication key. Thinking-title reuse is invalidated by value/metadata changes, detached detail DOM, or expansion changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; added tests directly count zero unchanged height measurements and one render across 20 identical titles.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Savings scale with long-running tool sequences and background activity frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression; these hunks fix repeated layout/markdown rendering work and were recorded as regression fixes where blame resolved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Responsive toolbars repeatedly move submenu and overflow actions in and out, then receive context updates.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Relayout creates/removes ActionBar view items and listeners synchronously; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is involved.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of responsive overflow/restore cycles and current dropdown count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single-toolbar relayout; listener disposal occurs with each pulled view item.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current dropdown subscriptions are keyed by live view item in a DisposableMap and disposed on pull/clear; no stale entries accumulate.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from ownership paths and repeated-overflow regression tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Memory benefit depends on resize frequency and toolbar lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff fixes unbounded obsolete dropdown/listener retention and was recorded as a regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: The chat input working border animates while active, resizes, becomes hidden, or reduced motion is enabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Two fixed mask elements use compositor transform animation; IntersectionObserver/document visibility pauses hidden animation. There is no external boundary.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live chat inputs with active working borders; two decorative nodes/gradients per input.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser compositor animations run independently; visibility management is shared by the base animation observer per window.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache; animation objects are CSS-owned and removed from active work when idle/hidden.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from fixed DOM/CSS selectors and visibility registration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GPU cost varies by input size and platform, but DOM cardinality is fixed per input.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff replaces animated gradient-property painting with fixed masks and transform rotation, clips overflow, and pauses hidden work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 35 changed files and relevant call paths. Submitted one medium cache-lifecycle finding for repeated Draw atlas regeneration after transient zero visibility. Recorded confirmed fixes for toolbar retention, persistent-footer measurements, and pet drag layout; the title-render fix could not be recorded because the regression-fix tool rejected that record twice.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
